summary: Camera-lock gate: by default returns 1 (lock allowed). If the occupant identifier stored at (vehicle array slot CurrentVehicleIndex) + 18580 differs from the one at (vehicle array slot CurrentPlayerIndex) + 18580, the camera is treated as unlocked: either the call is blocked (returns 0) when mode index a2 equals 3 and the gate flag byte_7CFE88 is clear while the byte at PlayerVehiclePtr+13388 is set, or the lock mode field at this+0x14 is set to -1 and 1 is returned.

local_names.a2: camera mode index (3 is the specifically gated mode)

operations.description: Initialize result to 1 (camera lock allowed) before any comparison.

Compare the occupant identifier at (dword_7C54F0[dword_7C54E4] + 18580) with the one at (dword_7C54F0[dword_7C54DC] + 18580); the rest of the body runs only when the two differ (player vehicle and current vehicle are different entities).
Mode-3 block gate: if byte_7CFE88 is zero and the byte at (dword_7C54E0 + 13388) is non-zero and a2 equals 3, return 0 immediately (camera lock denied).
Return 0 when the mode-3 block gate fires, before writing the lock field.
When the occupant identifiers differ and the block gate does not fire, set the camera lock mode field at this+0x14 (this[5]) to -1.
Return the default result (1, lock allowed) when the occupant identifiers match or the lock field was reset.

unresolved: Semantics of the constants 18580 (occupant-identifier offset within a vehicle slot) and 13388 (flag offset within the player vehicle pointer) are not evidenced.
The gate flag byte_7CFE88 and the meaning of mode 3 are caller-dependent and not evidenced here.
The comparison field at vehicle slots +18580 and the flag at PlayerVehiclePtr+13388 are read via global pointers; the write to this+0x14 is the only local state change.
